definitions.explanation: A short hand weight held in one hand for exercise, classically a solid iron piece. {鉄|てつ}アレイ is the older native term; ダンベル (from English) is now more common.

examples.japanese: {鉄|てつ}アレイで{腕|うで}を{鍛|きた}える。
examples.english: Train the arms with a dumbbell.

examples.japanese: {両手|りょうて}に{鉄|てつ}アレイを{持|も}つ。
examples.english: Hold a dumbbell in each hand.

examples.japanese: {毎日|まいにち}{鉄|てつ}アレイを{使|つか}って{運動|うんどう}すると、{少|すこ}しずつ{筋力|きんりょく}がつく。
examples.english: If you exercise with dumbbells every day, you gradually build strength.

notes:
{鉄|てつ} (iron) + アレイ. The traditional Japanese word for a one-handed exercise weight.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鉄|てつ}アレイを{持|も}つ: to hold a dumbbell
- {鉄|てつ}アレイ{体操|たいそう}: dumbbell exercises

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ダンベル: dumbbell — the more common modern loanword
- バーベル: barbell — a long two-handed bar
